title: Damaged item reporting and staff follow-up
lede: Reports now hold damaged gear consistently, preserve evidence, and give staff a clear place to inspect it before release.

sections.heading: After-only component evidence
sections.note: Sample data rendered with the actual ItemConditionReports component and compiled application CSS. Desktop and narrow-width states were inspected. No trustworthy authenticated before capture was available; no comparison is claimed.

changes.was: Web reports could save without a maintenance hold; damage could be submitted without evidence; old photos were deleted on replacement.
changes.now: Report, hold, and audit commit together. Damage needs a description or photo, including retained evidence. Conflicting in-flight edits return a conflict, and old evidence remains accessible through audit.

changes.was: Item detail did not expose the condition reports that explained the hold.
changes.now: Staff/admin see up to five recent reports with evidence, reporter, date, and checkout links. Reports remain visible when the hold is cleared.

changes.was: A blind toggle could reverse the intended state, and a stale inspection could miss new damage.
changes.now: Item detail asks staff to confirm inspection and sends an explicit desired status against the item version they reviewed. New damage updates that version. Legacy bodyless callers remain compatible.

verification: 83 focused tests passed across 10 files, including native API/source compatibility.
Eight new safety regressions fail against isolated copies of the original service and maintenance route.
TypeScript, edited-file lint, final application build, documentation verification, and diff whitespace checks passed.
No schema change, production data mutation, commit, push, or deployment.
notes: Authenticated browser/save proof is blocked by the unrelated pending Radio Clip migration 0156_radio_clip_sign_in in this branch preview.
Screenshots show an isolated static component, not the full item page. They do not prove persistence, notifications, actual damage photos, or the inspection confirmation interaction.
Native/list clients still use the legacy maintenance toggle; the explicit version guard is wired to web item detail.
No repair assignment, repair notes, or separate report-resolution state was introduced.
